LESSON: WRITING SYLLABLES (BA-BU, DA- DU),

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: READING 2.1 Print awareness (2 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learner
Topic 2.2: Writing Syllables (ba-bu, da- du),
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing Syllables (ba-bu, da- du),, part of READING 2.1 Print awareness (2 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learner in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Where can we read letter sounds from in and out of school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing Syllables (ba-bu, da- du), together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Love: The learner with the others in class correct each other positively as they make syllables.

• Responsibility: The learners peer teach one another on how to read syllables.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Where can we read letter sounds from in and out of school?

• Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner gains confidence in reading syllables.

• Learning to learn: The learner persists in learning to join sounds to make syllables.
